source.title: 周公解夢
source.attribution: 周公解夢, 維基文庫 contributors, revision 7907671. Adapted by RECATOOLS: each line split into dream and reading, converted to Simplified with OpenCC, English added. Released under CC BY-SA 4.0.

sections.en: Buddhas, Daoists, Monks, Nuns, Ghosts & Gods

en.k: The gate of heaven turns red
Face turned up to the sky
Riding a dragon up to heaven
Going to heaven to seek a wife
Climbing up to the sky or onto a roof

en.i: Fear that the realm will be divided

en.n: Wikisource reads 天愈鐃, which has no clear sense; it is probably a slip for 天欲曉 'the sky about to dawn'. The English follows that reading.

en.k: Sun and moon shine on you

en.i: Worry that a parent will die

en.k: Sun and moon about to rise
Sun and moon sinking behind the hills

en.i: A noble son will be born

en.k: The sun or moon enters your bosom
en.i: The sun, a noble son; the moon, a daughter

en.k: Worshipping stars and moon, burning incense

en.i: A noble son will be born

en.k: A shooting star that does not fall
Patrolling the sky, touching the stars

en.i: Lucky; blue or black ones unlucky

en.k: Snow does not touch your body
Black vapor rising from the ground
Climbing a cliff, holding a rock
Playing with a small stone in hand
Your body goes into the earth
A mountain crumbling as you climb
Finding wealth on a mountain walk
The floor of the hall caves in
Sitting or lying in a forest
A tree grows in the forest
A tree breaks while climbing it
A great tree falls onto a house

en.i: A person of rank shelters you

en.k: A tree grows in the hall
A fruit tree grows in the gateway
A pine grows from your belly
en.i: The rank of one of the Three Dukes

en.k: A pine grows in the home
A cypress grows in the house
A maple grows on the roof
Fruit trees heavy with ripe fruit
A heap of dung and dirt
Worms breed in a sick body
A cangue and lock put on you
Your body grows fat or thin
Two horns growing on the head
Hair and beard turn white and fall
Pus and blood from hands and feet
Shaving the head, cutting the hair
Brows as long as the hair
Teeth fall out on their own
Wearing an official cap and boarding a carriage
en.n: Wikisource reads 戴官 'wearing office', probably a slip for 戴冠 'wearing a cap'.

en.k: Putting on your own headcloth or cap
A benefactor gives you robes and cap
Changing into new robes and cap
A woman wears cap and sash
Holding a tablet to see a noble

en.n: Wikisource reads 笏硫, which has no clear sense; other copies read 笏破 'a broken court tablet'.

en.k: Giving someone a court tablet and seal ribbon

en.i: A wife or concubine is added

en.n: Wikisource reads 孛衣, probably a slip for 孝衣 'mourning dress'.

en.k: A wife wears her husband's clothes
Newly granted a title of rank

en.i: You are already out of danger

en.k: Banners and swords lead you into the mountains
Setting out with a drawn blade
Cut by a blade and bleeding
Stabbing someone with a broken blade
Wounding yourself with a blade or axe
Receiving a blade or axe from someone
A blade falls into the water
Traveling with a sword or blade
Whetting a sword to a keen edge
Giving someone a sword or blade
A sword at the head of the bed

en.n: Wikisource reads 鐘豉 'bells and fermented beans', a slip for 鐘鼓 'bells and drums'.

en.k: A drum with a fine sound
A drum that makes no sound
The emperor grants you a seat
Worshipping a Buddha that seems to move
Watching something laid out over a fire
en.n: The first half, 看火上陳, has no clear sense and may be corrupt.

en.k: Someone tells you that you are dead
Someone calling to you from outside
Paying homage at the imperial court
Meeting an immortal at a Daoist temple
Climbing a tower, pavilion or altar
Building a high tower at home
Pulled up onto the city wall

en.i: Unlucky; going out of the gates is lucky

en.k: Roofing a house atop the wall

en.i: Wealth; going out to the garden is lucky
A happy event for your wife

en.k: A boat breaking through the roof
Climbing the wall into a house
Disputing a house with a woman
The courtyard caves into a pit
Wife and sons beneath a wall

en.n: 死央 has no clear sense in Wikisource or in other copies; one copy reads 屋瓦落 'roof tiles fall'.

en.k: A horse born inside the house
Pine and cypress growing on the roof

en.n: Wikisource reads 大吉昂; 昂 is probably a slip for 昌.

en.k: Door panel breaks on its own
Pit or ditch before the door
A small door opens in the house
Digging a well and striking water
A well about to run dry
A sound from peering in the well
Drunk and falling in a well
Someone says to climb out of the well
A vessel falls into a well
In the privy, amid excrement and urine
Gold and silver made into vessels
Gaining a gold or jade ring
Arms full of pearls and jade

en.i: Good in spring/summer, bad in autumn/winter

en.k: Looking at oneself in a mirror

en.i: Your wife or concubine is deceitful
Husband and wife come to blows
A person of rank helps you
Your wife bears a lovely daughter

en.k: Bed curtains taken down and changed

en.i: Brought in, lucky; taken out, unlucky
Brought in, lucky; taken out, unlucky

en.k: Spreading a mat and sitting together
Suddenly holding a feather fan (text garbled)
en.n: Wikisource reads 毛肩 'hair shoulder', probably a slip for 毛扇 'feather fan'.

en.k: A basin whose bottom falls out
Getting into a basin or jar
A table set up in the house

en.n: Wikisource reads 碾衣食; other copies read 碾衣石 'a stone for pressing clothes', which fits this section.

en.i: You will gain power and rank

en.k: Viewing sun and moon from a boat
Sailing past the sun and moon
A sick person on a boat
Helping your father into a boat
Driving a cart on an outing
A sick person boards a cart
Going up a bridge hand in hand
Carts going over a bridge road
Husband and wife go to market
Husband and wife at a banquet
Husband and wife scolding each other
Husband and wife break a hairpin
A wife and husband go into water
Husband and wife comb each other's hair
Husband and wife bow to each other
Seeing a wedding and mourning together
A man turns into a nun
Eating beef in the main hall
Eating meat of a creature that died on its own

en.i: A noble son will be born
Your wife will bear a son

en.k: Eating greens and finding them yellow
Eating oil, salt, sauce and fermented beans

en.i: Bright is good, dim is bad
Growing is good, breaking is bad

en.k: A coffin comes out of the grave by itself
Carrying a coffin into the house
Opening a coffin and speaking to the dead
Laying a corpse in its coffin
Wearing the seal of a duke
Wearing a seal, holding a tally
A seal ribbon; a change of post
en.n: Wikisource reads 緩印; 緩 is probably a slip for 綬 'seal ribbon'.

en.k: Drawing a bow and the string breaks
Being given a bow and crossbow
Singing and music in the hall
Lying ill, helped up by others
A sick person crying or laughing
A sick person loading a cart
A dead person weeping in someone's arms
A dead person coming back to life
Seeing others die, or dying yourself

en.i: A happy event will be added

en.k: Seeing a late elder of the family
A Dharma master mounting the seat

en.n: Wikisource reads 真入 'truly enters', probably a slip for 真人 'a Perfected One'.

en.k: Entering a temple and the idol stirs
A monk teaching people to chant sutras
A Taoist priest or priestess speaking
Being beaten by gods or ghosts
Gods or Buddhas in the hall
A god or Buddha image without form
Welcoming gods in a festival rite

en.i: You will gain a noble son
Your wife will bear a son

en.k: Killing someone and bloodying your clothes
Burning the body and blood flowing
Wounding yourself with knife or axe

en.n: The second half reads 中二吉, whose sense is unclear.

en.k: Walking with your head cut off
Beaten by your wife or concubine

en.n: Wikisource reads 手措; 措 is probably a slip for 指 'finger'.

en.k: Killing an ox or a deer
Killing an ox and eating the meat
Slaughtering a donkey, mule, or horse

en.n: Wikisource reads 愛災 'love disaster', probably a slip for 受災 'suffer disaster'.

en.k: A thief goes to prison of his own accord
Chasing a thief and seeing him
A cangue and lock put on you
A cangue and chains entering the house
Going to court in a lawsuit
A clerk leads you into the office
Grain ears growing even and fine
Rice and wheat laid out together
Sitting or lying on rice and wheat
Getting grain, then suddenly losing it

en.n: The first character, 涓, is probably corrupt; other copies read 酒麴 'brewing yeast'.

en.k: Hemp growing thick as a forest
Being in the water at ease

en.i: Unlucky if you do not get out

en.k: River water with sand and stones
Fire burning the sun and moon
A great fire burning the sky
Walking the road with a torch
Burning a well with a torch
Fire breaks out in the kitchen
Lighting a fire while awaiting appointment
Led on by a wicked person
Chasing a thief into the market
en.i: Unlucky if he does not come out
Getting out is lucky; not getting out, unlucky

en.k: Washing your hair and moving house

en.i: You will be drawn into a lawsuit

en.k: Riding a dragon into the water
Riding a dragon up a mountain
Riding a dragon into the market
A dragon or snake entering the gate
A dragon or snake entering the stove
A snake turns into a dragon
en.i: A person of rank helps you
She will bear a noble son

en.k: A dragon or snake killing someone

en.n: Wikisource writes 蛟 'flood dragon' where the sense is 咬 'bite'.

en.i: You will bear a noble son
Quarrels; a green one is lucky

en.k: A phoenix lands on your palm
A crane rising to the sky

en.i: You will bear a noble son

en.k: A wild duck enters the house
A swallow flies into your bosom
en.i: Your wife bears a noble son
A guest from afar will come

en.k: A bird flies into your bosom

en.i: Office gained; if it crows, quarrels
Your fame will shake the world

en.k: A white elephant or river hog

en.i: You will gain a high seal of office
You will father a noble son

en.k: River deer and deer at home
A live hare in the garden
A white mouse leading the way

en.i: You will get what you seek

en.k: Rats running off in large numbers
A yellow ox comes to the house
Leading an ox up a mountain

en.i: You will rise to high office

en.k: A cow gives birth to a calf
Riding an ox into the city
A horse dancing in the courtyard
A horse galloping a thousand li
A horse carrying money and goods
Grooming, washing and releasing a horse
A herd of horses galloping away

en.i: Lucky; a pig that dies by itself is unlucky

en.k: A pig turning into a person
A sheep walking like a pig
Pigs and sheep scratching an itch
Riding a sheep down the street
A dog barks at its master
A horse born in the house
A turtle entering a well or home
Casting a net to catch fish
Angling for fish in the water
Fishing or hunting in a forest

en.i: Your wife is pregnant; very auspicious

en.k: Shrimp and frogs croaking and hopping

en.i: A child born in old age

en.k: A moth flies into the lamp
A silkworm moth flying off without a cocoon
en.n: Wikisource reads 蚤 'flea', almost certainly a slip for 蠶 'silkworm'.

en.k: Dung beetles gathering in a heap

en.i: Great luck for land and house
